lore:
The first time you saw a living golem was at the scholar lady's house.

"Even now, she still amazes me. To me, she is the universe itself."

The golem gave you a mechanical smile and muttered something incomprehensible. You gazed into her gray eyes and felt as though you had fallen into a surging gray ocean, its shimmering waves stretching from one horizon to the other.

Before you left, the scholar lady handed you a worn booklet containing notes on the creation of golems. That night, you spread it open and studied its scribbled formulas and spells, but your mind remained filled with the golem's elusive smile.

You could never forget her.

Several days later, you found an excuse to visit again. You stepped over piles of books, tools, and skeletons, pulled aside heavy curtains tangled with cobwebs, and finally crouched before the golem.

The scholar lady was huddled in a corner. In just a few days, she had become haggard and drained of light.

"You came... just like the others."

The scholar lady coughed weakly.

"Yes... I came."

You took the golem's hand and kissed it again and again.

Its cool fingertips brushed against your neck, causing a brief stab of pain. You closed your eyes.

When you awoke, warm white sunlight bathed you. Your body undulated in gentle waves.

You felt lighter than ever before, as though your soul had slipped free of your body.

You turned your head and saw gray-black heads.

They wailed and writhed like dark wildflowers scattered across a gray primeval ocean.

"No—"

Black mucus caught in your throat, and you could no longer move.

You realized that you had become one of those heads.

"In June of Year 2, the renowned alchemist Romalin Ludwig was found mysteriously dead in his study. His head was missing, and the mysterious alchemical manual had disappeared..."

—Recorded in Volume 2 of <Italic:Alchemy Anecdotes>, Mythag Library
